task.piece: The part of the engine interface the database needs, with no database in it: typed values and rows; a schema of the model written as the rows of the cortex's tables (schema/cortex) and read back from them; the numbered ids of the parts the model gives none, with their counters; an engine's own folder declared as data (its card, tables, rules, seeds and migrations, embedded) and its options written as the rows of its tables and read back; and the kit's checks of an engine's tables. Rows are plain values; nothing here opens PostgreSQL (the store does, t06). Nothing else: no file of an owner's folder changes, no engine implements the new part (t03, t04).
task.before: Merged on main: the model, the engine interface with the section layout and the kit, the MySQL engine; the spec check (t01); the owners' folders and their cards.
task.after: Quill (t03) and MySQL (t04) implement Tables and pass the kit's new checks; the store (t06) writes the rows of cortex_rows and of every engine's Tables into PostgreSQL and reads them back through cortex_schema and Tables::read.

The parts an object may have are its kind's, as the engine declares them in object_kind_parts
A schema written into the store and read back is the same schema: every part, every value, every order.

module.public: Value, Row, Rows, File, Migration, Identity, Tables, cortex_rows, cortex_schema, counter_id and the id functions of step 2; re-exported from crates/engine/src/lib.rs as pub mod tables; Engine gains fn tables(&self) -> Option<&dyn tables::Tables> { None }
module.step: A Value is Null, Bool(bool), Integer(i64), Numeric(String), Text(String), Uuid(String), Timestamp(String) or Json(String): Numeric a decimal as text (`1`, `2.5`), Uuid the 36-character form in lowercase, Timestamp RFC 3339 in UTC ending Z, Json the value as serde_json writes it compactly. A column's Value is the variant of its type in its table file: BOOLEAN Bool, INTEGER and BIGINT Integer, NUMERIC Numeric, TEXT Text, UUID Uuid, TIMESTAMPTZ Timestamp, JSONB Json; an absent optional value is Null. A Row is pub struct Row { pub table: String, pub values: BTreeMap<String, Value> }, table its full name (cortex.objects), its values by column name, the column id among them; Rows is pub type Rows = BTreeMap<String, Vec<Row>>, every row by table name, each table's rows in the order written. A File is pub struct File { pub name: &'static str, pub sql: &'static str }; a Migration is pub struct Migration { pub version: u32, pub name: &'static str, pub sql: &'static str }; an Identity is pub struct Identity { pub id: String, pub name: String, pub comment: Option<String>, pub created_at: String }, the schema_identity columns the model does not hold.

The id functions give the id of every part the model gives none, as the cortex's table files write them in their id comments and CHECKs, numbered from 1 in the order of the model: table_key_id(object, n) is `<object>.key<n>` (the primary key, when there is one, first, then the unique keys, then the identifier key), table_key_column_id(key, n) `<key>.<n>`, check_constraint_id `<object>.check<n>`, index_id `<object>.index<n>`, index_part_id `<index>.<n>`, index_include_id `<index>.include<n>`, partition_field_id `<object>.by<n>`, partition_id `<object>.partition<n>`, sort_field_id `<object>.order<n>`, enum_value_id `<object>.value<n>`, composite_type_field_id `<object>.field<n>`, routine_parameter_id `<routine>.param<n>`, trigger_event_id `<trigger>.on<n>`, object_tag_id `<object>.tag<n>`, object_read_id `<object>.read<n>`, relationship_column_id `<relationship>.<n>`, verbatim_statement_id `statement<n>`. counter_id(id) is the id without its trailing digits (`o_orders.key1` is `o_orders.key`, `o_orders.key1.2` is `o_orders.key1.`, `statement4` is `statement`). Rows written for a schema read in number its parts from 1 and hold, for every counter_id they used, one row of cortex.id_counters whose last is the greatest number given under it.

cortex_rows(schema, engine, identity) -> Result<Rows, String> writes the model and every slot of its sections into the rows of the cortex's model tables, every column of each table file holding a Value of its type: the one row of cortex.schema_identity from identity, the schema's engine and version, the schema section's format as section_format, and one true; cortex.object_kinds from engine.kinds() (id, name, position its place in the declaration) and cortex.object_kind_parts, one row `<kind>.<slot>` for each slot of each kind, the slot written as its name in snake case (Slot::PartitionOf is partition_of); cortex.namespaces, cortex.subject_areas, cortex.objects and cortex.relationships with position their place in the model's list; cortex.object_tags, cortex.object_reads, cortex.columns (position their place in the object; default_value, generated_expression and generated_stored from the column's section), cortex.column_identities (from the column section's identity), cortex.relationship_columns (the relationship's from and to columns paired by place) and the relationships' enforced, on_delete, on_update (the cortex's words: no_action, restrict, cascade, set_null, set_default), match_kind, deferrable and initially_deferred from the link's section; and from each object's section: cortex.table_keys and cortex.table_key_columns (primary, then unique, then identifier), cortex.check_constraints, cortex.indexes, cortex.index_parts (direction asc or desc, nulls first or last), cortex.index_includes, cortex.table_partitionings, cortex.partition_fields, cortex.partitions, cortex.partition_parents, cortex.sort_fields, cortex.view_queries, cortex.sequences, cortex.enum_values, cortex.domains, cortex.composite_type_fields, cortex.routines, cortex.routine_parameters (mode in, out or in_out), cortex.triggers (timing before, after or instead_of; on its table), cortex.trigger_events, cortex.scheduled_events; cortex.verbatim_statements from the schema's section, after_namespace when its after names a namespace and after_object when it names an object, else the error `statement <n>: it follows <id>, which is neither a namespace nor an object`; cortex.required_extensions from the schema's section; and cortex.id_counters (step 2). Every position is a Numeric of its place counting from 1. It writes no row of schema_migrations or of the log (the store's). A section that does not follow the layout is the error `<part id>: <the layout's message>`. An option in any section is not written here (it is the engine's, step 5).

cortex_schema(rows, engine) -> Result<Schema, String> is the inverse of step 3: the schema with its format the model's FORMAT, engine and version from the row of cortex.schema_identity, every part in the order of its position compared as a decimal, every section rebuilt in the layout from its rows, the schema section's layout the layout's LAYOUT and its format the row's section_format; options empty everywhere (the engine fills them, step 5). The rows of id_counters, object_kinds and object_kind_parts are not read into the schema. A row that refers to a part no row holds is the error `<table> <row id>: refers to <id>, which no row holds`.

Tables, the new optional part of Engine (Send + Sync), its folder declared as data, every text embedded with include_str!: fn card(&self) -> &'static str, its owner.toml; fn files(&self) -> &[File], its table files, each named by its table's full name (engine_quill.record_options), in name order; fn rules(&self) -> &[File], its rules/ files, each named by its rule; fn seeds(&self) -> &[File] { &[] }; fn migrations(&self) -> &[Migration] { &[] }, its versions from 2 up and, when there are, 1 its migrations/1_tables.sql; fn rows(&self, schema: &Schema) -> Result<Rows, String>, every option of every section of the schema as rows of its own tables, with the ids of step 2 for the parts they refer to and the cortex.id_counters rows of its own numbered ids, and the error `<part id>: option <key> has no column in <engine>'s tables` for an option it cannot place; fn read(&self, rows: &Rows, schema: &mut Schema) -> Result<(), String>, which puts every option back into the sections of a schema that cortex_schema made from the same rows.

The conformance kit checks an engine that has Tables, on every sample it is given: its card's namespace is `engine_<engine id>` and every file's table is in it, else `table <name> is not in <engine>'s namespace engine_<engine id>`; every row rows() writes is of one of its tables or of cortex.id_counters, else `rows() writes <table>, which is not one of its tables`; every value of a row is the variant of its column's type (step 1), else `<table> <row id>: <column> is not <type>`; and the round trip: the sample read, then cortex_rows (under an Identity of the kit's own) and rows() written, then cortex_schema and read() back, is the schema read, else `<sample>: its tables do not give back the schema read: <id>`, the id of the first part whose JSON differs, taken in the order namespaces, objects (each with its columns), links, areas, and `schema` for the schema's own fields and section. An engine without Tables is checked as before (t04 makes Tables required of an engine that reads).

tests.how: Rust tests on schemas built in each test with the model's constructors and the layout's types, under an engine of the test file's own that declares two kinds (one with Slot::Keys, one with Slot::Query) and no options; the cortex's table files are read from schema/cortex to know every table's columns and their types. No test reaches a database, the network or a file outside schema/cortex.
tests.prove: every value cortex_rows writes is the variant of its column's type in its table file
a position is a decimal, a flag a boolean, an absent optional value null
every id function gives the id the cortex table files require in their id checks, numbering from 1 in the model's order
a counter row is written for every counter id used, holding the greatest number given under it
every row cortex_rows writes is of a cortex table and names every column of that table's file and no other
object kinds and their parts are written from the engine's declaration, one part row for each slot of each kind
table keys are written primary first, then unique, then identifier, each with its columns in order
a section that does not follow the layout is an error naming its part
the identity row is written from the identity given, and a verbatim statement after a namespace or an object refers to it by the column of its kind
a schema with every slot of the layout filled, its section's format included, is written by cortex_rows and read back by cortex_schema as the same schema
every part comes back in the order of its position compared as a decimal, whatever order the rows are given in
a row that refers to a part no row holds is an error naming the table, the row and the id
the kit finds an engine table outside its namespace, a row of a table the engine does not hold, a value of the wrong type and a round trip that loses a value
